structure: Independent people sampled from a trivariate Gaussian population. The supplied means, variances and marginal X-Y correlation are preserved as population parameters. Both otherwise unspecified correlations with Z are assigned 0.5 as an explicit scenario.

parameter_provenance.basis: Exact population means in X, Y, Z order.
Covariance equals the reported Pearson correlation because both variances are one.
Unreported relationship; chosen scenario value, also equal to correlation under unit variances.
Unreported relationship; chosen scenario value, also equal to correlation under unit variances.
Convenient joint distribution consistent with the specified population moments; Gaussian shape is not established by the records.

requested_estimands.name: partial_xy_given_z
requested_estimands.basis: The Pearson correlation of the separate population OLS residuals is (rXY-rXZ*rYZ)/sqrt((1-rXZ^2)*(1-rYZ^2)). The selected correlations give (0.5-0.25)/0.75 = 1/3. Records A and C do not determine either correlation with Z.

requested_estimands.name: marginal_xy
requested_estimands.basis: Record A directly specifies the population marginal Pearson correlation.

requested_estimands.name: slope_x_on_z
requested_estimands.basis: The population OLS slope with an intercept is Cov(X,Z)/Var(Z). The chosen covariance and reported unit variance give 0.5; the covariance is not supplied by the records.

limitations: The partial correlation and X-on-Z slope are scenario values, not identified evidence-composition results.
Gaussian shape and the two correlations with Z are modeling assumptions, not measured facts.
Records constrain population moments. Random finite samples will fluctuate around them; the generator does not recenter, rescale, select or otherwise calibrate realized samples.
These are descriptive Pearson and OLS relationships in an artificial population, with no causal or clinical interpretation.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically checked that the selected covariance matrix has eigenvalues 2, 0.5 and 0.5, so it is positive definite.
Analytically checked that Cholesky transformation of independent standard normal innovations yields the specified population means and covariance.
Analytically evaluated the residual-correlation and OLS-slope formulas under the chosen scenario.
No Python execution or empirical simulation checks were performed.
